values.value: Anyone can become an Acrobat. Each Acrobat level grants +1 Move. Template A grants Dodge and Nah 1/day; Template B grants Tricky; Template C grants Cat Power and increases Nah to 2/day; Template D grants Roast the Oaf. Dodge gives +2 Defense per empty inventory slot, capped at 16 or 10 + Dex, whichever is lower, and does not stack with armor. Nah can declare once per day, or twice per day at Template C, that something physically dodgeable does not affect the Acrobat. Tricky makes a natural 20 attack deal double damage and grant a free combat maneuver; a natural 19 deals normal damage and grants a free combat maneuver. Cat Power treats falls as 20 feet shorter and causes cats to tend to like the Acrobat. Roast the Oaf lets the Acrobat force a larger enemy that misses with a melee attack to make another melee attack against a target in range, potentially itself. Two copies of Tricky from two Acrobat and two Fighter levels combine into Very Tricky.
values.rationale: Page 12 identifies Acrobat as an available class; pages 49–50 provide the class-selection rule, progression, and complete Acrobat abilities. The detailed class text is the canonical card content.

values.value: Anyone can become a Barbarian without first unlocking the class through play. Each level of Barbarian grants +2 Loincloth HP. Advancement grants Rage at A, Firewater at B, Thews 1/day at C, and Rampage plus Thews 2/day at D.
values.rationale: Page 12 identifies Barbarian as an available class, page 49 states that anyone can choose it, and page 51 gives its progression. The detailed progression supersedes the generic class-list sentence.

values.value: Anyone can become a Fighter without first unlocking the class through play. Each level of Fighter grants +1 Attack. Advancement grants Stand Tough at A, Tricky at B, Very Tricky at C, and Double Attack at D.
values.rationale: Page 12 identifies Fighter as an available class, page 49 states that anyone can choose it, and page 52 gives its progression. The detailed progression is the canonical class text.

values.value: In this introductory adventure, every player controls multiple level 0 peasants. They have no special abilities and die in a single hit; the multiple peasants give players extra lives while they learn the system. The game begins with 12 level 0 peasants in a dungeon; unless there are more than 6 players, each player controls multiple peasants, choosing one as their PC and treating the rest as hirelings.
values.rationale: Pages 2 and 5 describe complementary parts of the level-0 setup: their fragility and extra-life role, then the starting count and PC/hireling arrangement.

values.value: Anyone can become a Thief without first unlocking the class through play. Each level of Thief grants +1 Mastery and +1 Stealth. Advancement grants Luck at A, Opportunist at B, Preparation at C, and Snag at D.
values.rationale: Page 12 identifies Thief as an available class, page 49 states that anyone can choose it, and page 53 gives its progression. The detailed progression is canonical.

values.value: Escaping the Dungeon Is a Milestone

values.value: A character with a lobster claw is Favored by Vandoh. If all seven mummies are reassembled and returned, or close enough, the character who took the most initiative becomes Favored by Vandoh. If all ghouls are killed, the character whose left hand was possessed becomes Favored by Vandoh; Appendix D gives the full effect.
values.rationale: Pages 22, 32, and 37 describe distinct source triggers that grant the same named favor; the canonical effect records all three without inventing Appendix D mechanics.

values.value: The Abacus of Vandoh is a Treasure in 39 STONE EGG. Made from maple, shale, and lapis lazuli, it performs addition, subtraction, multiplication, and certain square roots. Three times per day it answers a question whose answer is an integer from 2 through 9; secretly roll d100, with 11–100 giving the honest answer, 2–9 giving the rolled number, and 1 or 10 giving no response. It cannot answer about things more than 100 feet away, only understands obdurate physical things, cannot read minds or understand names, struggles to distinguish humans, and cannot understand questions longer than 12 words.
values.rationale: Page 36 places the Treasure in the Stone Egg, page 43 supplies its mechanics, and page 54 confirms its Treasure status and location. The composed text preserves both placement and rules.

values.value: The robed skeleton in 14A SHADRAKUL offers a black iron spellbook. Its covers and pages are polished iron sheets with letters formed by unpolished sections; a chain is woven through the spine to secure it to the owner's waist. Written in Cheoxic, it lets a character begin learning Cheoxic, contains speak with dead and fear, and permits advancement as a Necromancer. Once the reader reaches Necromancer Level 1, Shadrakul asks that character to become her apprentice.
values.rationale: Page 24 establishes the encounter and location; page 43 supplies the spellbook's complete description and effects.

values.value: A vial of utterly black oil that bends light toward itself, produces a lensing effect in the surrounding air, and has no smell. Tasting it creates a large piercing-like hole in the tongue. Applied to a surface, it creates a hole up to 6 inches wide and 5 feet deep, never wider than half the object; created holes cannot intersect. Applied to a portcullis, it can make the bars resemble Swiss cheese without breaking them. Consuming it creates a hole in the abdomen and causes the consumer's guts to fall out.
values.rationale: Page 23 identifies the bottle as a Bone Pile Search result and page 43 gives the complete Liquid Hole mechanics; the appendix description is the canonical item text.

values.value: Liquid Hole
values.rationale: The appendix labels the item Liquid Hole; page 23's Bottle of Liquid Hole is the same item found in the dungeon.

values.value: The crone's coffer in 42 SUNKEN GALLERY contains the Treasure called the Hand Mirror of Lies. It is shaped like the outline of a woman's face, complete with ears and carefully styled hair. The holder chooses what appears in the mirror; it can display anything the holder imagines, including an honest reflection.
values.rationale: Page 38 establishes the location and Treasure status, page 43 gives the full item description, and page 54 lists it among the dungeon's Treasures.

values.value: A harpoon leans against the east wall in 33 FUNGUS. Harpoons are also suggested tools that can be combined with other tactics to kill the Lamb in the cistern.

values.value: Burning oil is a suggested weapon against the Lamb in the cistern, and the rowboat at 45 BARRELS contains 2 flasks of oil. Key light sources include 1 oil in room 5 and 2 oil each in rooms 24, 30, and 45.
values.rationale: Pages 41 and 54 describe oil's tactical use and its keyed dungeon quantities; the values are complementary rather than competing descriptions.

values.value: The armored corpse beyond the portcullis carries an Orb of Indulgence worth 500s. It is a silver orb about 1 inch across that immediately forgives the bearer's next significant sin, after which it corrodes. Orbs are sold but tightly controlled; the source says finding one makes resale to the Church the only ethical option. Rumors claim golden orbs can forgive even mortal sins.
values.rationale: Page 25 establishes the found item and value; page 43 supplies its mechanics, control, and rumor. The rumor is retained explicitly as rumor.

values.value: A purple pouch in 4 CHESTS and a small bag in 34 CACHE each contain 2 doses of purple lotus powder. When smoked, it causes 1d3 hours of sleep; on waking, the GM rapidly presents a fun dream, a dream of something that happened, a scary dream, and a dream of something likely to happen in random order, with at least one semi-useful. A smoker thereafter cannot sleep without more purple lotus powder unless they have remained sleepless for 3 nights.
values.rationale: Pages 21 and 34 record two separate dungeon caches, while page 48 gives the drug's complete mechanics; all facts concern the same item.

values.value: Ropes are suggested tools that can be combined with other tactics to kill the Lamb in the cistern. Key items include 30-foot ropes in rooms 18A, 31, and 40.
values.rationale: Page 41 describes the tactical use and page 54 lists the keyed rope supplies; the canonical text preserves both.

values.value: Akina carries the Ruby Ring of Wisdom, worth 1000s, and offers it in exchange for rescue. It is the Treasure in 8 PIT.
values.rationale: Page 23 establishes Akina's possession and bargain; page 54 confirms the ring's Treasure and 8 PIT placement.

values.value: The lead-and-iron chest in 4 CHESTS contains only the Skull of Davok, which escapes when the chest is opened. The remnant of the demon Davok resembles a deformed elephant skull. Once freed, it tries once per round to absorb flesh from one person within 30 feet (Cha Save or die), regrows much of its head and voice after absorbing flesh, demands to be carried out, and casts geas until obeyed. It can call a carpet of vermin to carry it at a crawl; if it wanders this way, add Davok to the Random Encounter Table in place of Atmospheric Encounters for rooms 1–20. It awakens when touched or when its name is called, casts ignite and polymorph with 3 MD, is stunned for 1 minute by 10 damage in one round while reconstructing, cannot be destroyed in this dungeon, and becomes inert if returned to its lead-lined chest. Once free it searches for its missing body parts and forces its loyal thrall into Davok's service.
values.rationale: Page 21 establishes the chest and release trigger; page 44 provides the Skull of Davok's complete behavior and mechanics.

values.value: A small bag in 34 CACHE contains 3 doses of toad shavings. When smoked, the user cannot move independently or take actions for 30 minutes, can speak with amphibians and reptiles, and experiences colors, patterns, and croaking noises as indescribably delightful.
values.rationale: Page 34 establishes the dungeon cache and quantity; page 48 supplies the drug's complete effects and duration.

values.value: Range 30 feet; target 1 effect; duration [dice] rounds. Delays an effect—something happening to one object because of an interaction with another object or spell. It can delay incoming damage or prevent a sword from breaking until later. It may be cast as a reaction outside the caster's turn and takes no time. The spell can create paradoxes, which the GM is encouraged to resolve in the way most painful to the caster.
values.rationale: Page 20 establishes that Father Bastoval knows Delay but prints no mechanics; page 45 provides the complete spell rules.
